headline: All majors below the 200-day line, funding positive but longs crowded, whales moving onto exchanges for the third straight week.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, with none of them sporting a golden cross. None. Bitcoin sits at 63,653, down 49% from its 12-month high of 124,773, while Ethereum is off 60.6% from 4,829. The smaller caps fare worse: Solana is down 70.4%, XRP down 67.7%, and DOGE down 75.7%. A market where every named asset is beneath its longer-term trend line is a market that has not yet turned; the tape does not lie about regime.

Momentum is mixed but skewed toward caution. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 47.4 and its MACD is below its signal line, suggesting neither strength nor recovery impulse. Ethereum reads 56.3 on RSI, a touch warmer but still not in overbought territory, and also MACD-negative. Solana's RSI of 42.7 is the weakest of the majors, and its MACD is below signal. Only BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal, but both are from weak bases: BNB's RSI is 48.3 and DOGE's is 40.7. The message here is that no major is showing strong upward acceleration. BNB's slight MACD advantage and DOGE's small tilt toward signal do not override the fact that both remain below their 200-day lines. When a full market is underwater and none of it has confirmed reversal momentum, pullbacks or temporary pauses are noise, not evidence of a turn.

Derivatives positioning shows longs are crowded and paying to hold the bet. Bitcoin funding is 0.42% per 8-hour period (4.6% annualized), Ethereum is 0.62% per 8-hour (6.8% annualized), and Solana is running 1.0% per 8-hour (11.0% annualized). Those are not extreme by historical standards, but they are positive across the board, meaning long positions are paying shorts to stay short. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio is 1.07, Ethereum's is 1.24, Solana's is 1.7, XRP's is 2.15, and DOGE's is 3.47. The smaller caps show pronounced long bias. Solana and XRP have seen more shorts liquidated than longs in their recent window, which can happen when the crowd is long and even a small move lower triggers cascade; DOGE saw more shorts liquidated too. Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen more longs liquidated, suggesting that as prices drifted lower, the over-extended long side bled. Open interest remains substantial: Bitcoin at 2.26 billion, Ethereum at 1.5 billion. The positioning is not extreme, but it is tilted and expensive, which means the structure is firm but the patience of longs is being tested.

Flows tell a tighter story. Over the last five sessions, Bitcoin spot ETF net inflows have persisted at 1,957.9 million, with six consecutive days of same-direction flow, and Ethereum has seen 777.3 million over the same window, also with six days of consistency. That is institutional bid from traditional finance, continuous and methodical. Against that, whale-scale Bitcoin movement over the last 24 hours shows 11.7 million net moving onto exchanges, specifically into Coinbase institutional. More important, the weekly whale flow data paints a three-week pattern of net movement onto exchanges: week ending August 11 saw 407 million onto exchanges, August 18 saw 438 million onto, and August 25 saw 963 million onto. The last week's print is the heaviest. This is not panic selling; it is deliberate accumulation-phase repositioning into institutional rails. The ETF bid is steady and large, whales are moving coins to institutional venues week after week, and stablecoin float at 308.7 billion is up 0.13% over 30 days and available as dry powder. The capital structure looks stable, even constructive at the margin.

Sentiment, measured by Fear and Greed, sits at 74 (Greed) with a 30-day range of 25 to 74. The gauge has swung hard within that range, and today it is in the upper half. Yet the tape shows a market where every major is below its 200-day line, funding is positive and crowding longs, and momentum has not confirmed any reversal. This is the disagreement to watch: the emotional gauge is greedy while the structural picture remains a bear market on the longer timeframe. Institutional flows are buying, but spot ETF flows cannot override the regime if it does not turn. Bitcoin network difficulty is retracting 1.3% at the next retarget, and fees are minimal (4 sat per byte fastest), indicating no on-chain congestion or urgency.

The condition that matters now is whether the majors can reclaim their 200-day lines. Bitcoin would need to move from 63,653 toward the historical resistance of its 200-day average; the same holds for Ethereum and the rest. Funding will remain worth watching if it begins to flip negative, signaling shorts gaining conviction. Watch also whether whale flows reverse direction away from exchanges, or whether they continue to deliver coins to institutional venues. An ETF inflow that persists while whales are positioning into exchanges is a configuration that can hold the line, but the regime will not confirm until price takes back the 200-day average. Until then, the market is a bear market at rest, not a recovery.
